subject: Astronomy & Space
title: Type Ia Supernovae: Standard Candles
description: A fast breakdown of Type Ia Supernovae: Standard Candles for builders.

hook.text: Type Ia supernovae all explode with nearly the same brightness. This makes them cosmic yardsticks for measuring distance.

buildup.text: They occur when a white dwarf in a binary system steals enough mass from its companion to reach a critical limit and detonate.

discovery.text: In 1998, two teams used Type Ia supernovae to discover that the universe's expansion is accelerating—a Nobel Prize finding.

twist.text: The consistent brightness comes from a fixed mass limit. Every Type Ia detonates at about 1.4 solar masses.

climax.text: These standard candles revealed dark energy—the mysterious force driving the universe apart faster and faster.

punchline.text: Same brightness every time. Dying white dwarfs showed the cosmos is flying apart.

quiz.question: What major discovery was made using Type Ia supernovae?
options: The universe's expansion is accelerating, revealing the existence of dark energy
Black holes exist at the center of every galaxy
The universe is much younger than previously thought

details.summary: Type Ia supernovae occur when white dwarfs in binary systems accumulate enough matter to trigger thermonuclear detonation at a consistent mass threshold.
details.whyItMatters: Type Ia supernovae led to the 1998 discovery that the universe's expansion is accelerating, implying a mysterious dark energy. This discovery earned the 2011 Nobel Prize and reshaped cosmology.
takeaways: White dwarf explosions triggered at a consistent mass threshold
Uniform brightness makes them reliable distance markers
They revealed the accelerating expansion of the universe

faq.question: Why are Type Ia supernovae all roughly the same brightness?
faq.answer: They explode when the white dwarf approaches the Chandrasekhar limit (about 1.4 solar masses), so each detonation involves a similar amount of fuel and releases similar energy. A correction based on how quickly they fade further standardizes their brightness to within 5-7%.

faq.question: How did they reveal dark energy?
faq.answer: In 1998, two teams measured distant Type Ia supernovae and found them dimmer than expected for a decelerating universe. This meant they were farther away than predicted — the expansion was speeding up. The unknown force driving this acceleration was named dark energy.
